nu -h.stdout:
The nushell language and shell.

Usage:
  > nu {flags} (script file) ...(script args) 

Flags:
  -h, --help: Display the help message for this command
  -c, --commands <string>: run the given commands and then exit
  -e, --execute <string>: run the given commands and then enter an interactive shell
  -I, --include-path <string>: set the NU_LIB_DIRS for the given script (delimited by char record_sep (''))
  -i, --interactive: start as an interactive shell
  -l, --login: start as a login shell
  -m, --table-mode <string>: the table mode to use. rounded is default.
  --error-style <string>: the error style to use (fancy or plain). default: fancy
  --no-newline: print the result for --commands(-c) without a newline
  --no-config: start with no config file. env: NU_NO_CONFIG=1
  --no-env: start with no env file. env: NU_NO_ENV=1
  --no-default-env: skip loading the default env config (default_env.nu). env: NU_NO_DEFAULT_ENV=1
  --no-default-config: skip loading the default config (default_config.nu). env: NU_NO_DEFAULT_CONFIG=1
  --no-vendor-autoload: skip loading vendor autoload files. env: NU_NO_VENDOR_AUTOLOAD=1
  --no-user-autoload: skip loading user autoload files. env: NU_NO_USER_AUTOLOAD=1
  --no-plugins: skip loading plugins. env: NU_NO_PLUGINS=1
  --no-history: disable reading and writing to command history
  --no-std-lib: start with no standard library
  -t, --threads <int>: threads to use for parallel commands
  -v, --version: print the version
  --config <path>: start with an alternate config file
  --env-config <path>: start with an alternate environment config file
  --lsp: start nu's language server protocol
  --ide-goto-def <int>: go to the definition of the item at the given position
  --ide-hover <int>: give information about the item at the given position
  --ide-complete <int>: list completions for the item at the given position
  --ide-check <int>: run a diagnostic check on the given source and limit number of errors returned to provided number
  --ide-ast: generate the ast on the given source
  --mcp: start nu's model context protocol server
  --plugin-config <path>: start with an alternate plugin registry file
  --plugins <oneof<list<path>, path>>: list of plugin executable files to load, separately from the registry file
  --log-level <string>: log level for diagnostic logs (error, warn, info, debug, trace). Off by default
  --log-target <string>: set the target for the log to output. stdout, stderr(default), mixed or file
  --log-include <oneof<list<string>, string>>: set the Rust module prefixes to include in the log output. default: [nu]
  --log-exclude <oneof<list<string>, string>>: set the Rust module prefixes to exclude from the log output
  --stdin: redirect standard input to a command (with `-c`) or a script file
  --testbin <string>: run internal test binary
  --compile <path>: compile a .nu file to bytecode (.nubc)
  --compile-user-lib: compile all .nu files in NU_LIB_DIRS to bytecode (.nubc)
  --compile-plugin-dirs: compile all .nu files in NU_PLUGIN_DIRS to bytecode (.nubc)
  --compile-std-lib: compile standard library prelude to bytecode
  --compile-startup-files: compile startup config files (env.nu, config.nu, autoload) to bytecode
  --compile-all: compile std-lib, user lib dirs, plugin dirs, and startup files to bytecode
  --clean: remove bytecode directory before compiling (use with --compile-all)
  --dump-bytecode <path>: dump bytecode (.nubc) file contents for debugging
  --dump-bytecode-json: output --dump-bytecode results as JSON
  --generate-completions <string>: output shell completions for nu (nushell, bash, zsh, fish, pwsh)
  --no-bytecode: disable loading .nubc for config files and sourced modules. env: NU_NO_BYTECODE=1
  --opt-level <int>: IR optimization level: 0=none, 1=peephole (default), 2=full multi-pass
  --opt-diagnostics <string>: emit optimizer diagnostics as JSONL to '-' (stderr) or a file path
  --experimental-options <oneof<list<string>, string>>: enable or disable experimental options, use `"all"` to set all active options

Parameters:
  script file <path>: name of the optional script file to run (optional)
  ...script args <string>: parameters to the script file

Examples:
  Run a script
  > nu myfile.nu

  Run nushell interactively (as a shell or REPL)
  > nu
